speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and tell me what your significant medical history consists of. We need to determine if these symptoms are progressive or sudden in onset.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like cerebellar dysfunction. To narrow this down, have you noticed any slurred speech, double vision, or difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning your shirt? Also, when did this imbalance first start, and have you had any recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the MRI report focusing on the cerebellum and brainstem for any signs of demyelination or infarction.

DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
